The changes included a tighter instruction and an extra downstream transform that may be suppressing clarifying questions — which plausibly increases hallucination risk for sparse clinical prompts. I attached a compact diff (promptset_v3_diff.json) and highlighted a few sample QA failures.

- If user-facing hallucination rate increases by >7% on critical slices (diagnosis mention, medication names) -> immediate rollback to control for affected customers.
- If overall precision drop >8% across production slice of >=2k examples -> rollback.
- Interim mitigation: enable reranking + stricter generation stop token for Acme in Dedicated/reserved route.

Quick update from research: ran 2k replay on Alice's attached slice and a 5k random sample from the production corpus. Findings:
- The v3 prompt rewrite increases literal completion length in constrained prompts; that appears to correlate with hallucination events when the model outputs unsupported diagnoses.
- Distribution shift: the problematic examples are concentrated in short-prompt clinical cases (<= 20 tokens instruction).
- Suggested experiment: run a reranking pass that penalizes hallucination-prone ngrams and measure delta on the 5k sample. Initial sim shows reranker reduces hallucination flags by ~6% but increases latency by ~30ms/req.

I'll upload the full run results to Drive; attached a short log snippet for context.
